units.translation: to lie awake

κοιμῶντες [lulling], for which Casaubon proposed καίοντες [burning], others have conjectured other things, Triclinius wrongly interprets as πραΰνοντες ἐπὶ τῷ ὀπτῆσαι ἢ θυμιᾶσαι [soothing for the purpose of roasting or burning incense]. More correctly Paleius; "as they put out the fragrant (cf. 819) incense-fed flame", probably by pouring wine upon it. Eur. Iph. T. 633 ξανθῷ τ᾽ ἐλαίῳ σῶμα σὸν κατασβέσω [with yellow olive oil I will quench your body]. Agam. 94 λαμπὰς – φαρμασσομένη χρίματος ἁγνοῦ παρηγορίαις [the torch – being drugged with the soothing of pure anointing]. The custom alluded to, of raising a shout at that particular point of the ceremony, though probable in itself, does not appear to be known from other sources.
